subject: english-language
title: Quotes, Dashes and Brackets
welcome_lead: Quotation marks frame speech. Dashes and brackets add aside.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on speech marks, dashes and brackets.
final_note: You can now punctuate dialogue and asides correctly.

concepts.def: Used for titles or quotes inside quotes.

walkthroughs.body_html: Put speech marks around exact words: 'Stop!' he shouted. Start a new line for each new speaker.
A hyphen joins words ('well-known'). A dash (longer, with spaces) shows a strong pause — like this.
Brackets hide a quick aside. Ellipsis trails off… leaving the reader to wonder.

options: Register is the same as accent.
A variety of language used in a particular social setting — varying by formality, field (topic) and mode (spoken/written) to suit audience and purpose.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
Register is just how loud you speak.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a phoneme and a grapheme?
options: Phonemes are letters and graphemes are syllables.
Phonemes are vowels and graphemes are consonants.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
A phoneme is the smallest unit of sound in a language; a grapheme is the written letter or letters that represent it.
Phonemes are vowels and graphemes are consonants.
Alternating between languages or varieties within a conversation or even a single utterance — often patterned by context, topic, identity or audience. Code-switching is rule-governed, not random.
Code-switching means using slang words in formal speech.
Code-switching shows the speaker doesn't know either language properly.
